lesson_title: The Tower on the Hill Changed Everything
hook_text: One tower went up near Lusikisiki. The clinic cheered, the shop cheered, and an elder frowned at the hill. All of them were right.
clip_script: In 2015 a cell phone tower went up on a hill near Lusikisiki. The clinic could call an ambulance in minutes. The school got internet. A son in Durban sent money home in seconds. The shop started taking cards. The farmer checked cattle prices before selling. Good news, and it is why the tower was built: designers asked the community what it needed and answered. But an elder frowned at the mast over the hill and the light that glows all night. Some people feared the radio waves. Children stared at screens till late. Thieves stole the batteries. Steel was smelted, concrete poured, a diesel generator smoked when Eskom cut out, and birds hit the guy wires. Technology always has two columns, good and bad, and they fall on different people. The designer's job is to list both honestly and then shrink the bad: solar instead of diesel, a disguised mast, shared towers. Not a perfect technology. A better balance.
visual_style: Whiteboard hill with a tower; two columns fill in beneath it, green ticks on one side and red marks on the other, then arrows from design fixes shrinking the red column.
mood: Thoughtful and fair, celebrating and questioning in the same breath.
pacing: Quick run of benefits, slower run of harms, then the two-column method and the fixes.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and write the two columns for a technology in your own home.
